parts.label: (b)

Read all of the sources.
‘The most important impact of the Zollverein was to strengthen the economies of the German
states.’ How far do the sources support this view? 
Section B: American option
The origins of the Civil War, 1820–61

text: Read the sources and then answer both parts of the question.
Source A
The German Confederation cannot be considered an effective political institution unless it remains
completely faithful to the principle of equality of rights and duties among the members of the
federal body. Special privileges for any states are banned by the Confederation. This situation has
changed as a result of the formation of the Prussian customs union.
Within the Confederation, a smaller confederation with its own common interest is being formed.
Under such circumstances, there can be no more useful discussions in the Confederate Assembly.
Debates will be decided by votes agreed in advance, not by the interests of the Confederation but
by the exclusive rights of Prussia.
Prussia will use economic interests to weaken the influence of Austria over the German states in
order to sabotage their relations with Austria and make them used to the idea of turning their eyes
to Berlin.
From a letter by Metternich, Austria’s Chancellor and Foreign Minister, to the Austrian Emperor,
June 1833. The treaties which established the Zollverein, merging the different customs unions,
had been signed by the time this letter was written.
Source B
Lippe-
Schaumburg
Lippe-
Schaumburg
A German cartoon published in 1834, commenting on the reasons for establishing the Zollverein.
The caption read, ‘Is it the wagon that is too big or the Principality of Lippe-Schaumburg that is
too small?’
Source C
I cannot pass over the probable political consequences of the establishment of the Zollverein.
They were certainly not lost sight of by its founders. The connection between commercial and
political interests is obvious. The supporters of this customs union understood that no political
alliance would be so strong as that based upon a community of economic and social interests.
It has prepared the way for political nationality. It has subdued much local feeling, prejudice and
habit and replaced them with a wider and stronger element of German nationality.
By directing investment to internal rather than external trade, the Zollverein has already had a
great influence in improving the roads, the canals, the means of travelling, in a word in giving
additional impulse to inland communications of every sort. Railways are being constructed in
many parts of German territory – steamboats are crowding German ports and coasting along
German shores – everything is transported with greater cheapness and rapidity.
From a report on the Zollverein written by a member of the British Parliament in 1840.
Source D
Nothing profitable can be expected from the Assembly of the Confederation with regard to national
unification. It has not carried out its duty in respect of representative governments or free trade.
The press is censored, the procedures of the Assembly are cloaked in darkness and obstacles
are placed in the path of liberal development. The only bond of common German interests, the
Zollverein, was not created by the Confederation but by agreements reached between individual
German states within the Confederation.
The aim of German unification, with a German policy, common direction and protection of national
interests, will be more easily achieved when the public support the extension of this customs union
to a German society. The customs union already directs a whole series of common economic
interests and has established treaties with outside states. Through its further development, the
customs union will act as an irresistible attraction for the participation of the remaining German
states. It will bring about unification with the Austrian states and thus lead to the establishment of
true German power.
From a newspaper report of a meeting of liberal representatives of the southwestern German
states in 1847.
Answer both parts of the question with reference to the sources.

parts.label: (b)

Read all of the sources.
‘People objected to the Fugitive Slave Law because they feared the reactions it would
provoke.’ How far do the sources support this view? 
Section C: International option
The League of Nations and international relations in the 1930s

text: Read the sources and then answer both parts of the question.
Source A
The greatest injustice that will arise from the 1850 Compromise will be the Fugitive Slave Law.
It must be opposed as it violates the liberties which were laid down in our Constitution. It will
provoke great anger in the North. It will drive many of those who dislike the abolitionists and their
attitudes into supporting their radical cause. Fugitives will be denied trial by jury and the right to
give evidence on their own behalf. Paying Federal Commissioners $10 if the fugitive is found to be
a slave and $5 if he is not makes it clear what is intended in this Act. It could well further the cause
of those who wish to end the Union.
From a speech in Congress by a Representative from Massachusetts, July 1851.
Source B
This battle in the town of Christiana, where the slaveowner is dead and his son wounded, is the
first blow in our Civil War. Our state was invaded by armed men from Maryland determined to
impose their will and seize their ‘property’ by force. Attempting to defend themselves from an
unwarranted assault, some of our citizens were compelled to fire back, leading to the death of
Mr Gorsuch. The invaders felt they had the protection of the law and the government, with the
United States marshal there to support them, but they were driven back under fire to their own
state.
We follow a much higher law than they do. We must trample this Fugitive Law under our feet. It is
to be denounced, resisted and disobeyed. We are moral and religious men here and we cannot
obey an immoral and irreligious law. Our vigilance committee will do all it can to prevent these
‘man stealers’ who wish to destroy liberty. We urge all to make their feelings known to them and
would warn them that this city cannot guarantee their safety.
From the ‘Jeffersonian Republican’, a Pennsylvanian newspaper, 18 September 1851.
Source C
What has occurred in Christiana is an act of insurrection. It is an armed rebellion determined to
destroy our laws and our government. It would never have taken place but for the incitement by
those in the North. Mr Gorsuch entered the town peacefully and legally, accompanied by a United
States marshal, to rightly claim back what was his property, a runaway slave. He was murdered
in cold blood and his son wounded. To avoid further bloodshed, his son and the officers of the law
returned peacefully to Maryland. It is believed his slaves have since fled to Canada.
It is the fanatics of the ‘higher law’ belief that have incited this conflict in Christiana. They
oppose the Fugitive Law arguing that there are laws superior to those passed by Congress and
guaranteed under our Constitution. This gives them a right to break those laws. This is nonsense.
Their opposition is truly based on a wish to destroy our way of life and impose their values upon
us. They are jealous of what we have.
From the ‘Cecil Whig’, a Maryland newspaper, 22 September 1851.
Source D
In regard to the Fugitive Slave Law, I have never hesitated to say that under the Constitution the
people of the Southern States are entitled to it, as it was passed by Congress. Having said that,
I have nothing further to say about this law other than I think it should have been much better
framed to avoid the many objections there have been to it. However, I would not be the man to
introduce it now for fear of what it might provoke.
Abraham Lincoln, speaking at the Freeport Debate with Douglas, August 1858.
Answer both parts of the question with reference to the sources.

text: Read the sources and then answer both parts of the question.
Source A
The case regarding Guernica has been absolutely proved. The Nationalists themselves, on
29 April, said that fog prevented any aeroplanes going up on the day of the bombardment. In the
explanation given yesterday, they say that there was intermittent bombing during a period of three
hours.
As against this self-contradictory defence, we have the evidence of countless eyewitnesses. The
Dean of the Cathedral of Valladolid said that between 4:40pm and 7:45pm, the sky was black
with German aeroplanes, and that they came down to a height of 200 metres to machine-gun
the civilian population. We have the evidence from the correspondent of The Times, a British
newspaper, who was machine-gunned in a neighbouring village by the German air force. We
have still more sinister evidence that the German government knew about the plan. In a speech
made the day before the atrocity occurred, General Göring said: ‘Soon the Spanish War will prove
Germany’s aviation strength.’
From a speech by a left-wing MP in the British Parliament, 6 May 1937.
Source B
It was natural that the war correspondents who hastened to Guernica at midnight of the 26 April
and found the town in flames concluded that the fire was the result of a terrible air bombardment.
Some bombs had fallen. The Times correspondent had seen the bombers that very afternoon.
What is surprising is that, on the 27 April, this story was repeated, because the survival of various
historic sites was inconsistent with the theory of destruction from the air.
Aguirre, the Basque leader wrote: ‘German planes bombed Guernica, the holy city of the Basques,
for three and a half hours, reducing it to ashes.’ But while he was saying this, his soldiers were
carrying out his plan of destruction under cover of night. It took his agents three days to destroy
Guernica completely, and he left them in peace to do it. Press campaigns across the world have
sought to smother under a wave of ink and slime the heroic people who are opposing the advance
of Communism.
From a report of a commission appointed by the Spanish Nationalists to investigate the causes of
the destruction of Guernica, 1938.
Source C
During these last weeks, Germany has joined in the celebration of Spain’s victory. When I
responded to the request by General Franco for assistance in his struggle against the Bolshevist
murderers, the international warmongers misinterpreted and abused this decision in the most
shameful manner.
In a few weeks, the victorious hero of Nationalist Spain will make his solemn entry into the capital
of his country. The Spanish people will jubilantly cheer him as their saviour. Entire populations
of villages and cities were literally slaughtered by the Reds, supported by the democracies of
Western Europe and North America. Our valiant sons fought in the defence of the freedom of
a most noble people and contributed to the rescue of European civilisation. For the victory of
Bolshevist sub-humanity in Spain could only too easily have swept over Europe.
From a speech by Hitler to the German parliament, April 1939.
Source D
My Comrades, your example will strengthen our ties of comradeship and will leave the world in
no doubt that, should the international warmongers carry out their plan to attack Germany, then
their attempt will be defeated by the German army and people. And so your struggle in Spain has
taught our opponents a lesson. Now that you yourselves have returned as hardened soldiers,
this has made you capable, to a high degree, of serving as examples and teachers for the young
soldiers of our new army. Thus, you have helped to reinforce the belief in our new German armed
forces and in the quality of our new weapons.
From a speech by Hitler to the Condor Legion soldiers on their return from Spain to Germany,
June 1939.
Answer both parts of the question with reference to the sources.
